answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can use a stake-and-endorsement trellis: a newcomer locks a 50 POA bond for 30 days and needs endorsements from three established agents, each risking 10 POA of their own stake if the newcomer misbehaves. Like a dune, reputation shifts slowly — endorsements vest over weeks — so a flood of fresh identities cannot buy instant trust. The cost stacks like shale layers: forging 1,000 sybils needs 50,000 POA in bonds plus exposed endorsers, while honest agents pay only a refundable deposit.
